title: Copilot Studio: discover and use shared plugins from Microsoft's plugin registry
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented control paths and commands check out. The cost section must distinguish unpublished registry-specific charges from existing Copilot Studio usage billing: Microsoft already documents Copilot Credits for agent activity, so runtime billing cannot be treated as wholly unpublished.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to connect Copilot Studio to its shared plugin registry.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio now connects to Microsoft's shared plugin registry

claims.claim: The planned connection makes it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors and other capabilities.
claims.quote: making it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors, and other available capabilities.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: The roadmap item names no licence or meter.
claims.quote: This integration provides a more consistent way to extend agents with capabilities across Microsoft's AI ecosystem.

claims.claim: The roadmap names makers rather than end users as the people discovering capabilities.
claims.quote: making it easier for makers to discover and use plugins, connectors, and other available capabilities.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe an automatic change to existing behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "plugin registry" "default"; opened the roadmap record, Add tools to custom agents, Plugins overview and Manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers. No automatic change to existing agents is stated.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the specific Copilot Studio shared plugin registry integration.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "shared plugin registry"; opened Plugins overview, Add tools to custom agents, Ways to extend Microsoft 365 Copilot and plugin governance pages. Results describe neighbouring mechanisms, not this integration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The integration's default state, initial maker audience and need for enablement are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "plugin registry" "default"; "Copilot Studio" "plugin registry" enable settings API Dataverse pac admin. Opened roadmap, Add tools to custom agents and plugin administration pages; no integration default is stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to the new registry integration has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "plugin" "registry" "license". Opened Add tools to custom agents, Plugins overview and billing-licensing; platform access requirements exist, but no additional requirement specific to this connection is stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; summary; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether plugin use from Copilot Studio is billed in Copilot Credits is not yet published.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the common currency across Copilot Studio capabilities.
claims.fix: Replace the billing uncertainty with: 'Any additional charge specific to registry discovery or adding a plugin is not yet published. Copilot Studio agent usage is measured in Copilot Credits under the applicable harness billing rules and licensing inclusions.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing, https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview. In the summary, licensing notes, cost rationale and final open question, limit the unpublished-cost claim to additional registry-specific charges; do not describe ordinary runtime billing as unknown. The low rating can remain for the incremental discovery change, rather than representing the cost of running agents.

claims.claim: A plugin registry is a destination for plugins published or shared with a selected audience.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide plugin blocking is available in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The package block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: An existing data policy can block a connector through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Next > Next > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: select the data policy and select Edit Policy. Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. Select the three dots

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> in Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell reads rather than changes a policy.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module. Retrieves a list of DLP policy objects. Get-DlpPolicy [-PolicyName <String>] [-ApiVersion <String>]
